# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pāṭidesanīya 1 (Bu-Vb Pd1)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pd1
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pāṭidesanīya 1
**Title (English, from literature):** The training rule on receiving a nun’s food

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭhamapāṭidesanīya* is the first rule in the *Pāṭidesanīya* chapter of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Vinaya Piṭaka. According to the rule, a Buddhist monk who receives food from a nun must formally acknowledge the offense. In secondary scholarship on the institutional history of monasticism, the rule is cited from the Vinaya Piṭaka's Suttavibhaṅga when discussing monastic community relations involving nuns [Falk]. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Direct parallels appear in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, along with Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Upāli-paripṛcchā traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan texts.
